# @arki/journal

> A journal for Drizzle entities. Every change is one normal table row and, when the entity's events are stored (the default), one immutable event row, written in one transaction. Projections run inside that transaction. Effects run after the commit, from a job table.

## Import paths

<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/journal`: `BATCH_LIMIT`, `COMMAND_FAILURES`, `CommandConflict`, `CommandForbidden`, `CommandInvalid`, `CommandNotFound`, `JournalError`, `LIMIT_BOUNDS`, `LIMIT_BUSY_REASONS`, `LIMIT_KEY_TTL`, `RUN_FIELD_LIMITS`, `RUN_OVERRIDE_LIMITS`; and 160 more.
- http/* (2 paths): The HTTP response cache on Postgres: `@arki/http/idempotency` stores a finished response here and replays it when the same `Idempotency-Key` comes again. `@arki/journal/http`, `@arki/journal/http/webhooks`.
- one path each: `@arki/journal/pg`, `@arki/journal/foreman`, `@arki/journal/dot`, `@arki/journal/errors`, `@arki/journal/contract`, `@arki/journal/orpc`, `@arki/journal/projection`, `@arki/journal/event-map`, `@arki/journal/testing`, `@arki/journal/event-log-contract`, `@arki/journal/postgres`, `@arki/journal/kurrentdb`, `@arki/journal/zod`.
<!-- llms:end -->

## Rules that bite
- The door is `journal.bind(db, meta)`: bind once per request or job, then `run(command, input)`. You give `meta`; the library never picks an actor.
- A rule that rejects a request returns a failure, typed from `journal.run`, and the command rolls back. Return a child's or `events` failure from the handler. Ignoring one throws `IGNORED_FAILURE`. To handle a refusal on purpose, use `accept(result)`. An oRPC app adds `commandErrors()`.
- A command declares its events: `{ writes: [OrderPaid] }`. An undeclared event fails with `BAD_DEFINITION` and nothing commits.
- Await every `write` and `run`. One journal operation per transaction at a time. No `Promise.all` over writes.
- `drain` and `worker` take the root database, never a transaction. Run the worker where its effects have their listeners.
- An effect lists the services it needs with `need<T>()`. Plain apps give them in `j.compose({ services })`; a Dot feature uses `needsOf` and `journalHandlers`.
- An effect has no `run`. To run a command on an event, start a `j.task` or `j.workflow` with `startOn`, and `startOn.timing` is required.
- A reducer returns the value the database will store, or the write fails with `VALUE_MISMATCH`. `null` deletes the row.
- Version 1 means created by the journal. A row from before starts at version 2. `adopt` gives it version 1.
- Events are stored unless the entity says `events: 'transient'`. A transient entity has no history verbs: they throw `NO_HISTORY`. `workflow.run` always stores its events.
- Another store: `events: log`, `postgresEvents` or `kurrentEvents` (no `-` in the kind, no `forget`). A log outside the transaction is forwarded; history verbs throw `FORWARD_PENDING` until it ran. Switching stores is a migration with `copyLog`.
- Pass ids exactly as stored. Events are frozen: copy before you change.
- A workflow step runs at least once. The step body owns idempotency: pass `ctx.key` to the provider. Compose workflows once per `initJournal()`.
- `.waitFor` waits for an app event and takes each event once per run. It stores a pointer, so `forget` reaches it. The table is `workflow_waits`.
- `limits: { transitions }` caps a run at 1000 by default. A node past the cap does not run; the run ends `failed` with `WorkflowTransitionLimit`.
- A step's returned failure fails the step, unless it is listed in `failures` with `onFailure: 'continue'`.
- `def.settled` and `def.startAndWait` take the root database and wait at most 30 seconds (above 0). A wait never cancels the run.
- `.parallel` runs branches as child runs; `'all'` gives an object by branch, `'any'` the first to complete.
- A `.command` node commits its command with its checkpoint: exactly once.

> The design spec (`docs/specs/2026-10-09-journal-design.md`) explains intent. `src/api.ts` defines the signatures. When they differ, `src/api.ts` is right.
